newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASTRA SEES LOSEC SHARE OF SALES FALLING.
newsitem.headline: ASTRA SEES LOSEC SHARE OF SALES FALLING.

text.p: Swedish drugs group Astra said on Friday it expected sales growth to pick up again next year and that its blockbuster anti-ulcer drug Losec's share of total sales should start to fall from now on.

"We have a 30 percent rate of increase for Prilosec (Losec in the U.S.) and we are launching Pulmicort in the U.S., plus that we have a number of new products in Europe. We should see a significant increase (in growth) already next year," Mogren said.
When asked when Losec's part of Astra's total sales would start falling, Mogren said it should start as of now.

In the first six months of the year, Astra's own sales of Losec rose 17 percent to 10.12 billion crowns while its total drug sales rose 13 percent to 21.47 billion, making Losec's part of total sales 47 percent.
Mogren again referred to the growth that the company expects for Pulmicort when it is launched on the U.S. market this autumn.
The market for asthma treatment of Pulmicort's kind is currently fairly small in the U.S. but Astra expects it to explode when Pulmicort moves in.
